compressible_pressure_origin: raw solver field P_comp_raw.pt (no ruler, k_c = Ra*Pr exactly)
tensor_layout: (N, 4, ny, nx) float32; channels [u_x, u_y, T, p]; row index = y (row 0 bottom), column index = x (col 0 hot wall); y_j = j/(ny-1)

formulas.common_units: free-fall: velocity U = sqrt(g*beta*dT*L), pressure rho0*U^2, temperature T/T0 -- BOTH members solved in these scales (Boussinesq member: genData_v6, coefficients sqrt(Pr/Ra), 1, 1/sqrt(Ra*Pr)); no unit change applied
formulas.velocity: identity for both (u_in = u_B in free-fall units, u_tgt = u_c); vel_factor = 1
formulas.temperature: identity for both (stored as T/T0 in [0.4, 1.6], eps = 0.6); range asserted
formulas.pressure_deramp: for each field fit p01(x,y) ~ a + b*y by least squares over the 64x64 field, y = row/(ny-1); r = p01 - (a + b*y) (zero-mean residual)
formulas.pressure_sign: the generator's Boussinesq weak form uses '+ p*div(v)', the opposite of the paper's, so the raw Boussinesq pressure is the negative of the paper's P: P_in = -(p_raw_B - mean). The compressible member keeps the paper sign: P_tgt = +Ra*Pr*(p_raw_C - mean).
formulas.pressure_center: spatial mean subtracted from P_in and P_tgt after scaling (m_in, m_tgt recorded)
formulas.approximation: raw_both: none on the scale (both members exact); the pair is asymmetric because only the compressible member carries a hydrostatic ramp.  raw_both_deramp: the linear-in-y fit is applied identically to both, which is symmetric but also removes physical linear-in-y dynamic-pressure content from each member.
formulas.pressure_scale: INPUT: the RAW Boussinesq solver pressure (P_bouss_raw.pt, units rho0*alpha^2/L^2) is used directly, s_B = 1, no ruler -- the corrected buoyancy Pr*Ra*(T-T0)/dT leaves no hydrostatic ramp.  TARGET: the RAW compressible solver pressure (P_comp_raw.pt, units rho0*U_c^2) is used directly too, s_c = 1 -- NO RULER ON EITHER SIDE.  The only operation on the target is the unit change k_c = Ra*Pr, which is exact rather than the per-sample (1/Fr^2)/|b_c| estimate the ramp ruler had to make from a min-max-normalised field. Both members are de-ramped with the same least-squares linear-in-y fit, which removes the compressible hydrostatic stratification and the (physical) linear-in-y part of both dynamic pressures.  This is the like-for-like variant, directly comparable with the v2 ramp_ruler and v3 raw_bouss_deramp datasets.

summary.b_B_is_slope_of: raw Boussinesq pressure (expected ~0: no hydrostatic ramp)

normalization.note: Phase 3 fills per-channel min-max over the union of input and target of the training split
